title: Relationship Pricing on Auto Loans: How the Reduction Is Earned and How Reductions Stack
content:
Piedmont Crescent Bank prices an auto loan partly on what else the borrower holds with the bank. The relationship reduction the product publishes is granted at funding where the borrower holds, on the funding date, an active checking account of a tier the product names as qualifying.

**Once granted, it is fixed for the life of the loan.** It is not added later if the qualifying account is opened after funding, and it is not taken away if that account later closes.

**How the two reductions sit together.** The automatic-payment reduction and the relationship reduction stack by simple addition, up to the ceiling on all reductions the product publishes, and never take the rate below the floor the product publishes. Any part of a reduction cut off by the ceiling or by the floor is lost; it is not carried over to a later date or to another loan.

**The relationship reduction and the standing draft instruction.** The relationship reduction is unaffected by anything that happens to the standing instruction to draft the installment from a checking account.

## Withdrawn basis

The basis by which, on cancellation of the standing draft instruction, the rate rose by the automatic-payment reduction actually applied and a later re-enrolment restored it is **no longer in force**. The basis in force for restating the rate when that instruction changes is the current one for Auto Loans.

## The evidence the grant rests on

Whether the borrower held a qualifying checking account is read from the bank's own record of that customer's checking accounts, as it stood on the funding date, and the account must have been in active status on that date. The account is correlated to the loan by the customer who holds both. A statement by the borrower that they hold such an account does not settle the grant.

## How the grant reads at the edges

An account of a qualifying tier opened one day after the loan funded earns nothing on that loan, because the test is made on the funding date. An account of a qualifying tier closed one year after the loan funded takes nothing away, because the reduction was fixed on the funding date.

Where the two reductions added together would take off more than the ceiling the product publishes, the rate is reduced by the ceiling and the remainder is lost. Where the reduced rate would fall below the floor the product publishes, the rate is set at the floor and the remainder is lost.
